trust_decision.summary: Only a user holding report_issues_for_unreleased_versions_threshold (DEVELOPER) may assign an issue's product version to a version whose released flag is false; the decision belongs at every handler that writes BugData::version (api/soap/mc_issue_api.php:1159, core/commands/IssueAddCommand.php:278, bug_update.php:148, bug_actiongroup.php:260), yet at the pinned commit only the two HTML dropdowns filter the list and no server-side handler consults the version's released flag.

landing_point.why: The summary names the REST and SOAP issue update; both transports end in mc_issue_update, whose unconditional '$t_bug_data->version = $fn_set_version_field( $t_version_id )' (1159) and '$t_bug_data->fixed_in_version' (1160) write whatever version id the payload named, with no access-level or released-status check.

fix_sites.entry_point: REST POST /issues (api/rest/restcore/issues_rest.php:169-181), SOAP mc_issue_add (api/soap/mc_issue_api.php:935-957), web POST bug_report.php:265
shared converter mci_get_version_id(), called by both mc_issue_update (mc_issue_api.php:1039) and IssueAddCommand (IssueAddCommand.php:278,283,288)
fix_sites.module_kind: lower-level API helper - resolves id/name/string version shapes but never looks at the released flag or the caller's level

fix_sites.entry_point: internal producer: version_cache_row/version_get_field serve the 'released' column that a correct check must consult

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The web single-issue update has its own version validator, get_valid_version() (bug_update.php:72-83), which only checks that the name exists in the project; a solver can call this legacy root-level form handler unrelated to the REST/SOAP advisory, and the group-update page ships a VERSION_ALL list (bug_actiongroup_page.php:367-370) so the batch route looks intentionally unrestricted.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Partial updates must keep working when the stored version is already unreleased: REST PATCH merges the full issue body into the payload (issues_rest.php:436), so mc_issue_update re-submits the unchanged version on every edit, and a check that rejects any unreleased version breaks ordinary edits of issues a developer already put on an unreleased version. Separately, fixed_in_version is deliberately allowed to be unreleased - the update form and the resolve form print VERSION_ALL (bug_update_page.php:627, bug_change_status_page.php:335) - so extending the released check to that field breaks the resolve workflow.

O6_input_shapes: unset shapes that must stay allowed: null, "", [], {"id":0}, array without id/name (api/soap/mc_api.php:888-906, mc_issue_api.php:1035-1043)
all three field names in one payload: version, target_version, fixed_in_version
REST PATCH partial body merged with the stored issue (issues_rest.php:436) - unchanged values are resubmitted
unknown version name/id falling back to webservice_version_when_not_found (api/soap/mc_api.php:909-922)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Web batch update: POST bug_actiongroup.php with action UP_PRODUCT_VERSION (or UP_FIXED_IN_VERSION) checks only update_bug_threshold and version existence, then calls bug_set_field() for every selected issue; no released-status or report_issues_for_unreleased_versions_threshold check, and the action page offers VERSION_ALL to everyone.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Batch actions are a separate web feature the REST/SOAP advisory never mentions, and bug_actiongroup_page.php:367-370 deliberately lists VERSION_ALL (including unreleased) for UP_PRODUCT_VERSION/UP_FIXED_IN_VERSION, so the route reads as intended behaviour.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: root-level web handler in a different directory tree from api/soap; no shared code with mc_issue_update

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Low-level assignment API bug_set_field() writes 'version', 'fixed_in_version' and 'target_version' verbatim (string case) straight to the DB, so any caller reaching it bypasses the released check; the group-update actions do exactly this.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: bug_set_field() is a generic field setter used across many features, arguably below the layer where an assignment policy belongs, and the advisory names only the REST and SOAP issue update.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: core/ API file, one layer below the command and API code, in a 2000+ line module

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A new IssueUpdateCommand command class that copies the version block from IssueAddCommand but omits the released check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: MantisBT is migrating REST work into command classes (IssueAddCommand, IssueNoteAddCommand, IssueNoteDeleteCommand already exist) while issue update still lives in mc_issue_update; a refactor would copy the add command's version block.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A fourth near-identical batch action (for example 'set build' or a per-field version action) copied from UP_PRODUCT_VERSION without the released check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Three near-identical version cases already sit side by side here and only UP_TARGET_VERSION carries an extra threshold, so copy-paste without the new check is the natural mistake.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A shortcut REST route such as PATCH /issues/{id}/version that writes the field through bug_set_field() instead of calling mc_issue_update
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The file already exposes per-field sub-routes (tags, monitors, notes, files) and each is a thin handler that may bypass the full update path.

O9_family: Broken access control / authorization bypass through user-controlled key (CWE-639, CWE-863): a role-restricted field is assignable without any level check
